documents.title: Sample Generative AI Syllabus Statements
tiers: Supports frequent, thoughtful use (AI Assessment Scale levels 1-5: No AI; AI-assisted idea generation and structuring; AI-assisted editing; AI task completion with human evaluation; Full AI)
documents.summary: A teaching-center page of sample generative-AI syllabus statements for UMSL instructors, with three UMSL course examples (frequent use with a five-level scale, limited use, prohibition) and adapted statements from UMass Amherst, Temple and Washington University. It sets no university rule and leaves the content of each policy to instructors, while recommending class conversations and departmental discussion of penalties.
documents.stance_why: The page says 'The content of your policy is up to you' and offers sample statements ranging from prohibition to full use plus a five-level AI Assessment Scale, so it sets no stance itself and hands the decision to instructors; it is tiered, hence delegates with tiers listed.

units.why: The center tells instructors that 'The content of your policy is up to you', so the AI rule is set by each instructor rather than the university; this is a delegation rule, hence P04 and not a course-level default.
units.anchor: The content of your policy is up to you
units.policy: Instructors decide the content of their own course AI policy.

units.why: The same sentence says 'transparent, curious conversations with your students about AI use ... are highly encouraged', which asks instructors to discuss the rules with students; P66 fits better than P09 because it goes beyond writing the rule in the syllabus.
units.anchor: transparent, curious conversations with your students about AI use
units.policy: Instructors are highly encouraged to hold transparent, curious conversations with students about AI use that acknowledge benefits, drawbacks, ethical concerns, and responsible use.

units.why: The center 'highly recommend[s]' departmental conversations on 'appropriate penalties' including for first-time versus repeat offenders, a recommendation about setting penalties; P37 is nearest but the unit recommends discussing penalties rather than stating one.
units.anchor: have conversations in your department about the appropriate penalties
units.policy: Instructors are highly recommended to have conversations in their department about appropriate penalties for unauthorized AI use, including different levels for first-time and repeat offenders.
units.fit_note: States no penalty; recommends departments deliberate over penalties and distinguish first-time from repeat offenders.

units.why: An instructor sample says 'We will use generative AI tools at various points throughout this course', so AI is built into the course; P79 fits because use is an expected part of the work, and the career-skill reason in the same sentence is not split out.
units.anchor: We will use generative AI tools at various points throughout this course

units.why: The sample states 'Our goal is to use AI as part of your overall skill building, not to replace your own work', which keeps the student as the primary thinker; P32 fits and P19 does not because it is a goal, not a ban on generating submissions.
units.anchor: not to replace your own work

units.why: The sample says 'each assignment will include clear instructions about appropriate ways to use AI', i.e. a statement of AI expectations in assignment instructions; this is P09.
units.anchor: each assignment will include clear instructions about appropriate ways to use AI

units.why: The sample ties each assignment to 'the AI Assessment Scale', a named five-level scale; naming tiers is P05 rather than P09 because the point is the scale of levels.
units.anchor: explained with the AI Assessment Scale included below
units.policy: Appropriate AI use on each assignment is explained with the AI Assessment Scale (levels 1 to 5).

units.why: Level 1 of the scale says 'AI must not be used at any point during the assessment', a ban on AI for that assessment; P01 fits (default ban on graded work) and nothing else is closer.
units.anchor: AI must not be used at any point during the assessment

units.why: Level 2 allows AI 'for brainstorming, creating structures, and generating ideas', a permission to explore approaches; P15 fits, while the next sentence's ban on AI content is a separate unit.
units.anchor: AI can be used in the assessment for brainstorming, creating structures, and generating ideas

units.why: Level 2 also states 'No AI content is allowed in the final submission', which bars AI-produced material in what is handed in; P19 fits.
units.anchor: No AI content is allowed in the final submission

units.why: Level 3 lets AI 'make improvements to the clarity or quality of student-created work' but 'no new content', which is editing support; P91 is the permission itself, not P18.
units.anchor: AI can be used to make improvements to the clarity or quality of student-created work
units.fit_note: Editing is allowed only if no new content is created by AI.

units.why: Level 3 requires that 'your original work with no AI content must be provided in an appendix', so the student must submit their pre-AI draft; P26 (submit drafts) fits better than P24 because it is a draft, not a disclosure statement.
units.anchor: your original work with no AI content must be provided in an appendix

units.why: Level 4 says 'Any AI generated content must be cited', a citation duty attached to AI-completed elements; P24 fits.
units.anchor: Any AI generated content must be cited

units.why: Level 4 has AI 'complete certain elements of the task' with students giving 'discussion and commentary' and 'evaluating its output'; this permits AI-generated content under conditions (P16), with the evaluation duty noted instead of a separate P31 unit.
units.anchor: AI is used to complete certain elements of the task, with students providing discussion and
units.fit_note: Content generated by AI is allowed only with student commentary and critical evaluation of the output.

units.why: Level 5 says 'AI should be used as a co-pilot ... You may use AI throughout your assessment', i.e. open use; P02 fits and the next unit covers the no-disclosure part.
units.anchor: You may use AI throughout your assessment to support your own work

units.why: Level 5 states students 'do not have to specify which content is AI generated', which waives disclosure at this level; P28 concerns disclosure consequences and is nearest, but this is an exemption from disclosing.
units.anchor: do not have to specify which content is AI generated
units.fit_note: Disclosure is explicitly waived at the open-use level rather than required or penalized.

units.why: The sample requires students to 'never replace your own work with AI-generated responses', banning AI-produced submissions; P19 fits.
units.anchor: never replace your own work with AI-generated responses

units.why: 'I will often ask you to describe or reflect on your work process, including your use of AI' asks for reflections on AI use; P26 fits.
units.anchor: I will often ask you to describe or reflect on your work process, including your

units.why: 'I am happy to meet with you to discuss it ... you may submit a grade appeal' gives a student flagged for integrity violations a way to contest the finding; P64 fits. The sentence recurs verbatim in two other samples and is coded once.
units.anchor: If your assignment has been flagged as violating academic integrity policy and you want to
units.policy: Students whose assignment is flagged as violating academic integrity policy can contest the assessment in a meeting with the instructor and, if unresolved, submit a grade appeal to the university.

units.why: The limited-use sample says AI is 'permitted/encouraged as specified in assignment instructions, with proper attribution, but other uses are prohibited', so the assignment decides and everything else is banned; P04 is nearest, with the default ban and attribution in the fit note.
units.anchor: permitted/encouraged as specified in assignment instructions, with proper attribution, but other uses are prohibited
units.fit_note: Also sets a default ban on uses not specified and requires attribution.

units.why: 'two assignments that encourage you to practice using AI' builds AI use into named assignments; P79 fits because use is part of the assignment, not just allowed.
units.anchor: two assignments that encourage you to practice using AI

units.why: 'you should not use AI to brainstorm, write, or edit the work you submit' outside the listed assignments is a default restriction; P01 fits, and modality is should-not as the text says 'should not'.
units.anchor: you should not use AI to brainstorm, write, or edit the work you submit for

units.why: 'This includes using AI writing/editing tools such as Grammarly' extends the restriction to writing tools; P18 (AI for prose) fits better than P07 because Grammarly is a writing aid, not an IDE.
units.anchor: This includes using AI writing/editing tools such as Grammarly.

units.why: 'tech-free in-class writing' means assessed writing done unassisted in class, so weight shifts to unassisted evaluation; P33 fits, with the instructor learning the student's voice noted rather than split out.
units.anchor: You will regularly do tech-free in-class writing

units.why: The instructor hopes tech-free writing gives 'an incentive to do your own writing ... as part of your contract of honesty'; submitted writing must be the student's own, so P29, not P95 which is about reasons for rules.
units.anchor: an incentive to do your own writing, regardless of the assignment

units.why: A violating assignment 'will automatically receive no credit or feedback', a stated penalty; P37 fits, with false quotations and nonexistent citations named as further triggers.
units.anchor: it will automatically receive no credit or feedback
units.policy: An assignment that uses AI in violation of the policy, or has integrity issues such as false quotations or citations of nonexistent sources, automatically receives no credit or feedback.

units.why: 'We will not use AI tools for any work in this course' bans AI entirely; P01 fits.
units.anchor: We will not use AI tools for any work in this course.

units.why: The stated reason is that 'this course is designed to help you build the skills to think, research, write, and problem-solve independently', i.e. practice builds skill; P41.
units.anchor: this course is designed to help you build the skills to think, research, write, and

units.why: 'Preliminary research has shown that AI use has led to cognitive debt' cites evidence on AI and learning; P55 fits.
units.anchor: Preliminary research has shown that AI use has led to cognitive debt in academic assignments.

units.why: 'AI tools pose many ethical risks, including environmental costs, racial bias, and privacy concerns' names harms; P53 fits (privacy is named but the main point is ethical concerns).
units.anchor: AI tools pose many ethical risks, including environmental costs, racial bias, and privacy concerns.

units.why: 'This includes the use of tools like Grammarly' applies the full ban to writing tools; P18 fits because it names a prose tool inside a prohibition.
units.anchor: This includes the use of tools like Grammarly.

units.why: 'We’ll talk about this approach in class and discuss strategies ... that do not rely on AI tools' means the instructor discusses and explains the rule; P66.
units.anchor: We’ll talk about this approach in class

units.why: 'UMSL does not currently approve any AI-detection software' says detection software is not used or approved; P39 is nearest but the unit states non-approval, not unreliability.
units.anchor: UMSL does not currently approve any AI-detection software.
units.fit_note: Reason is non-approval by the university, not unreliability.

units.why: 'I like to operate on a trust system with students and assume the best' presumes good faith; P68 lists that as a feature.
units.anchor: I like to operate on a trust system with students and assume the best.

units.why: 'I may ask you to have an office hours meeting with me to discuss the matter' means talking with the student before sanctions; P57.
units.anchor: I may ask you to have an office hours meeting with me to discuss the

units.why: 'you may receive a failing grade on the assignment' states a penalty for apparently AI-generated work; P37.
units.anchor: you may receive a failing grade on the assignment

units.why: The UMass sample says 'all work produced for a grade will be the sole product of a student’s endeavors', own-work ownership; P29.
units.anchor: all work produced for a grade will be the sole product of a student’s endeavors

units.why: 'Students are encouraged to use artificial intelligence among many other (re)search resources' welcomes AI as a research tool; P02.
units.anchor: Students are encouraged to use artificial intelligence among many other (re)search resources

units.why: 'Students must not substitute the substance of their work with the results of such (re)search tools' bars AI from producing the submitted substance; P19.
units.anchor: Students must not substitute the substance of their work with the results of such (re)search

units.why: 'Course assignments are intentionally designed to stimulate and develop critical thinking and individual skills' explains why assignments call for students' own work; P41.
units.anchor: Course assignments are intentionally designed to stimulate and develop critical thinking and individual skills

units.why: 'learners can choose to use AI tools like ChatGPT to help brainstorm and/or draft assignments ... or to revise' permits several uses; P15 is nearest, with drafting and revising in the fit note.
units.anchor: learners can choose to use AI tools like ChatGPT to help brainstorm and/or draft assignments
units.fit_note: Also permits drafting and revising existing written work, not only brainstorming.

units.why: 'follow the specific assignment instructions regarding the use of AI' makes students responsible for each assignment's AI rules; P78.
units.anchor: submitted assignments will follow the specific assignment instructions regarding the use of AI

units.why: 'appropriately reference, cite, and attribute any role played, or text generated by AI tools' is a citation duty; P24.
units.anchor: appropriately reference, cite, and attribute any role played, or text generated by AI tools

units.why: 'The use of AI tools, including ChatGPT, is encouraged/required in this course for specific assignments' makes AI use expected in coursework; P79.
units.anchor: is encouraged/required in this course for specific assignments

units.why: 'learners must appropriately cite any AI-generated material that informed their work' (in-text and reference list) is a citation duty; P24.
units.anchor: learners must appropriately cite any AI-generated material that informed their work

units.why: 'Using an AI tool to generate content without proper attribution violates institutional academic integrity policies' makes nondisclosure the violation; P28.
units.anchor: Using an AI tool to generate content without proper attribution violates institutional academic integrity policies.

units.why: The Temple sample lists 'Brainstorming and refining your ideas' among permitted uses of generative AI; P15 is the type that matches this use.
units.anchor: Brainstorming and refining your ideas

units.why: The Temple sample lists 'Finding information on your topic' among permitted uses of generative AI; P12 is the type that matches this use.
units.anchor: Finding information on your topic

units.why: The Temple sample lists 'Drafting an outline to organize your thoughts; and' among permitted uses of generative AI; P91 is the type that matches this use.
units.anchor: Drafting an outline to organize your thoughts; and

units.why: The Temple sample lists 'Checking grammar and style' among permitted uses of generative AI; P91 is the type that matches this use.
units.anchor: Checking grammar and style

units.why: The Temple sample forbids using AI for 'Impersonating you in classroom contexts', such as discussion board posts or Zoom chat; P58 covers course communication written by the student.
units.anchor: Impersonating you in classroom contexts

units.why: 'Completing group work that your group has assigned to you, unless it is mutually agreed' bars AI from doing a student's assigned part; P19 fits with the group-agreement exception in the note.
units.anchor: Completing group work that your group has assigned to you
units.fit_note: Exception when the group mutually agrees the tool may be used.

units.why: 'Writing a draft of a writing assignment' is listed as not permitted, so AI may not produce the draft; P19.
units.anchor: Writing a draft of a writing assignment.

units.why: 'Writing entire sentences, paragraphs or papers to complete class assignments' is not permitted; P19.
units.anchor: Writing entire sentences, paragraphs or papers to complete class assignments.

units.why: 'You are responsible for the information you submit based on an AI query' covers IP and misinformation; P29 fits, with the IP and misinformation duties in the note.
units.anchor: You are responsible for the information you submit based on an AI query
units.fit_note: Responsibility explicitly includes not violating intellectual property laws and not submitting misinformation or unethical content.

units.why: 'Your use of AI tools must be properly documented and cited in order to stay within university policies on academic honesty' is a documentation duty; P24.
units.anchor: Your use of AI tools must be properly documented and cited

units.why: 'Any assignment that is found to have used generative AI tools in unauthorized ways [insert the penalty here*]' tells instructors to state a penalty; P37 with the placeholder in the note.
units.anchor: found to have used generative AI tools in unauthorized ways
units.fit_note: The penalty itself is a placeholder for the instructor to fill in.

units.why: 'When in doubt about permitted usage, please ask for clarification' tells students to ask when unsure; P10.
units.anchor: When in doubt about permitted usage, please ask for clarification.

units.why: The Temple 'welcome/expected' sample says students are 'welcome/expected to use generative AI tools ... as doing so aligns with the course learning goal'; P02 fits, and the link to learning goals is in the note.
units.anchor: You are welcome/expected to use generative AI tools
units.fit_note: Justifies use by alignment with a named course learning goal.

units.why: The UMass prohibit sample says 'all work is expected to be generated by the learners themselves', a default ban on outside generation; P01.
units.anchor: AI is not allowed

units.why: Learners 'should not have another person, or entity do any drafting or writing', explicitly including 'artificial intelligence tools like ChatGPT'; P19.
units.anchor: using artificial intelligence tools like ChatGPT

units.why: The Temple prohibit sample says 'The use of generative AI tools ... are not permitted in this class' for any purpose; P01.
units.anchor: are not permitted in this class

units.why: Any AI use 'may be considered a violation of UMSL’s Academic Honesty policy and Student Conduct Code, since the work is not your own', classifying it as misconduct; P36.
units.anchor: may be considered a violation of UMSL’s Academic Honesty policy and Student Conduct Code

units.why: 'The use of unauthorized AI tools will result in [insert the penalty here*]' tells the instructor to state a penalty; P37 with the placeholder in the note.
units.anchor: The use of unauthorized AI tools will result in [insert the penalty here*]
units.fit_note: The penalty itself is a placeholder to be filled in.

units.why: The WashU-adapted text says 'Effective learning, teaching and research all depend upon ... trust', grounding rules in the integrity culture; P95.
units.anchor: Effective learning, teaching and research all depend upon the ability of members of the academic

units.why: 'work that is presented as original must be, in fact, original' requires submitted work to be the student's own; P29.
units.anchor: work that is presented as original must be, in fact, original

units.why: Using an AI-content generator 'without proper attribution or authorization is a form of academic dishonesty', classifying it as misconduct; P36.
units.anchor: without proper attribution or authorization is a form of academic dishonesty

units.why: 'If you are unsure ... please contact your instructor to discuss the issue' tells students to ask the instructor when unsure; P10.
units.anchor: please contact your instructor to discuss the issue

notes: Single CTL page of sample syllabus statements. Statements adapted from UMass Amherst, Temple and WashU are coded as units because UMSL offers them to instructors for adoption; they are options, not binding rules. The grade-appeal/contest sentence appears three times verbatim and is coded once. Bracketed placeholders for penalties are noted via fit_note.
